correctness.rationale: At prime p occurring to exponent exactly one in n=pm, U(n)=(p+1)U(m) and T(n)=pT(m), so equality forces p=U(m)/(T(m)-U(m)); there is at most one p per cofactor m. Partitioning by largest prime p>y and whether p occurs once gives E(X)≤Psi(X,y)+floor(X/y)+X sum_{p>y}p^(-2). The Rankin estimate with alpha=1-1/log y and the prime-harmonic upper bound yields Psi(X,y)≤C X exp(-logX/log y)(log y)^e for y≥e^4. Taking y=exp(sqrt(logX)), X≥e^16, gives the stated X(logX)^2 exp(-sqrt(logX)) bound, since e/2<2. The argument is logically valid and handles n=1. Original verify_equality_sparsity.py computes the small equality list; that finite list is not substituted for asymptotic proof.
